title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription
abstract: arXiv:2610.33004v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. In this work, we investigate entitylevel analysis of OCR errors as a complementary perspective for evaluating OCR quality in historical documents. Using a publicly available benchmark of 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive, augmented with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that will be released upon acceptance, we compare sequence-recognition OCR systems, OCR-specialized vision-language models, and general-purpose vision-language models. Beyond global transcription accuracy, we analyze entity preservation and recoverability under varying character-level edit tolerances. translated_title: 面向历史文档转录的实体感知OCR系统评估
translated_abstract: 光学字符识别（OCR）对于历史档案数字化至关重要，然而字符错误率（CER）等标准评估指标并不一定能反映姓名、日期和标识符等有意义的信息是否被保留。在本工作中，我们研究了OCR错误的实体级分析，作为评估历史文档OCR质量的一种补充视角。我们使用来自Berrutti档案的175份文档的公开基准数据集，并辅以5,209个手动标注的实体提及（将于论文被接收后发布），比较了序列识别OCR系统、OCR专用视觉语言模型以及通用视觉语言模型。除了全局转录准确率之外，我们还在不同的字符级编辑容差下分析了实体的保留性和可恢复性。我们的实验表明，OCR系统的排名取决于评估标准：虽然Qwen 3.6在……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出以实体级错误分析作为OCR评估的补充视角，并基于包含5,209个手动标注实体提及的历史档案基准证明，OCR系统的排名取决于评估标准，传统字符错误率等指标无法反映姓名、日期等关键信息的保留情况。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes entity-level error analysis as a complementary perspective for OCR evaluation, demonstrating on a benchmark of 175 historical documents with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that OCR system rankings depend on the evaluation criterion, since standard metrics like CER do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information such as names and dates is preserved.
